This is the first launch introduction. It will walk you through some of the main features in project intelligence. If this is not your first time here then feel free to skip this intro.  Most features in PI are pretty self explanatory but there are a few less obvious features you may find useful.

This is just a general overview of some of the different ways you can use PI. As you have probably already figured out you can open PI by pressing %s.  PI Also has an "Explain This" function which allows you to press %s while hovering your mouse over an item in an inventory to view any documentation related to that item. You can also press %s to view available documentation for a block or entity you are looking at in world.  PI GUI Notes: Whenever you open the main PI UI you will return to the previous page you had open. When you open PI for the first time in a session you will get the "Home Page" by default this is the Project Intelligence mod page but you can change this by right clicking on a page in the page list and selecting the "set as home page" option.

This gui is extremely customizable! You can find the style settings by pressing the options button in the top right corner of PI. There you will find some builtin style presets and an option to edit the current preset which you can then save as your own custom preset!

This is an open source project created by brandon3055. The goal of this project is to create a truly universal documentation mod by leveraging the power of the minecraft community.  So how will this work? well for starters any mod developer can add documentation for their mods to PI. The problem is mod devs are busy people so most of them wont have time to deal with something like this and that in my opinion is a major issue with most of the current documentation mods.  PI aims to solve this problem by making it possible for anyone in the community to contribute by writing documentation for various mods using the relatively simple built in editor. They can then submit their documentation via PR and if it passes review it will be added to the online repository.
Please be aware as all project intelligence documentation is stored online the mod requires internet access to function correctly.
On first launch PI will download and cache all available documentation pages for the installed mods. Any images are downloaded and cached on an as-needed basis to reduce internet usage.

Welcome to the main interface of the mod. The first thing suggested to do is to use the two buttons in the upper right to input the recipes, which allows you to create and edit recipes. All of the calculations require recipes to be recorded.\fTo calculate the cost of an item, simply pick the item from JEIs item list then put it in the slot in the upper left of the interface with all of the recipes to use recorded. The result will then be displayed in the lower slots of the interface. The four buttons provide options to display input, output, catalyst and crafting steps.\fThe button in the upper left allows you to edit and get a label. Labels are a very important part of the mod. They are basically things that can be put into a slot, including ItemStack, FluidStack, OreDict entry, or simply a placeholder. Lables are used in the calculation process. Most of time they are quite clever as long as you configure them properly.

This interface allows you to import recipes. First place exported data files into "config/JustEnoughCalculation/data/", then you will see them in the list organized as "filename/group" if there is no error (otherwise check the log). Use the buttons to select recipe groups to import and hit the tick, then you are done.\fFor pack makers or server owners, you can rename the data file and place it at "config/JustEnoughCalculation/default.json" to set it as default. When player creates world or joins server, the default recipes will be automatically setup for the user.

This interface allows you to create labels. This mod provides 4 types of labels: fluid, oreDict, placeholder and item. To create fluid and oreDict label, you can just search and pick. Item labels represent an item stack, but with fuzzy options for meta, nbt and capalibity.\fAs is indicated by the name, Placeholder labels do not hold any content. It is just a string to connect recipes. You can use it for anything, like structure or event energy. To create one, simply type in the name, then hit the tick. You can also search and pick from existing ones.

You can use both buttons and keyboard (numpad or main keyboard) to use it. For main keyboard, the buttons are mapped to these keys:
- plus: = or +
- minus: - or _
- times: ' or "
- divide by: / or ?

This interface allows you to create or edit recipes. To create one recipe, you can pick items from the JEI item list, then put it into the slots. When finished, simply click the save button. You can also fast transer recipes from JEI by clicking "+" when openning recipe view.\fTo edit one label, you can simply click it, then a toolbar will pop up to help you, where you can switch between amount and percentage mode, type the amount, or remove the label. In addition, you can use mouse scroll to quickly change the amount. Clicking the "Clear" button will remove all of the labels.\fUsing recipe fast transfer, some labels will automatically setup for you, like oreDict labels. If you do not want this behavoir, simply use "Disambiguous" button to select manually. You can also add labels by ckicking the "Add label" button. By the way, normally you shouldn't put fuzzy labels as output.\fYou can easily manage recipes using groups. Click the "New group" button, type the group name and hit the tick, you are done. The new group name will show in the top bar. If you already have groups set up and you want to use an existing one, you can use the arrows to select between them.\fWhen you are editing an existing recipe, you will have two extra buttons, "Save as" and "Delete". "Save as" allows you to save the current recipe as a new recipe, without changing the existing one. "Delete" simply allows you to delete the recipe.

The last stand enchantment uses your XP bar as a final protection against dying.\n\nWhen you reach 0.5 hearts, the game will take XP from you whenever you're damaged instead of killing you. The higher number of enchantments you have the cheaper the XP cost will be.

Everyone can make mistake. But with §L/ob_inventory§R command you can fix some of them. This command can be used to restore inventory. Backup is created when:
 - player dies
 - grave is spawned 
 - player issued command §L/ob_inventory store§R

To restore inventory you need backup name. Go to folder below or to saves folder on server and look for files named §Linventory-*.dat§R. Then restore inventory with §L/ob_inventory restore <player> <id>§R - where id is either full filename or just middle part, without §Linventory-§R and §L.dat§R. You can also use tab completion. Backups are normal NBT files and can be opened with any editor.
